output.text: PICK: (b) 'noticed {{company}} isn't really running TikTok Shop lives'. REASON = RELEVANCE, not proof strength. Both openers carry the identical proof (Willow Boutique $126k last month from interactive livestreams), so proof strength is a wash — the only variable is relevance. (b) is a first-person, manual-looking observation ABOUT THIS PROSPECT (their own uncaptured gap) — it reads hand-written, aimed, rung 2-3, and passes QA Q10 (speaks TO them). (a) 'most fashion brands pay Meta...' is a third-person category THESIS with the market as subject — QA Q10 auto-fail (statement-lead / podium voice), the rung-0 'blast' read. (a) is the L1 Go Fish shape on the same client + same offer that lost and drew STOPs; (b) is logged winner W18 (Evergreen id 21): human replies + a converted call from 360 sends.

variants.t1: Hey {{first_name}}, it's Bri at Go Fish - a bit random but noticed {{company}} isn't really running TikTok Shop lives, we actually tried it for Willow Boutique, who sold $126k last month just from interactive livestreams with relevant creators.
variants.t2: not asking for your business but could I at least share a few ideas on how {{company}} could take advantage of this?

variants.winner_ref: W18 Go Fish / Evergreen copy id 21 (human replies + converted call from 360 sends)
variants.loser_ref: L1 Go Fish = opener (a) shape, category brag; why_it_failed = 'whole text is about US / a market thesis, zero relevance hook tying it to THIS recipient' -> STOPs
variants.mechanism: interactive TikTok Shop livestreams with relevant creators (simple support; relevance is what carries)

trace.result_summary: Both map to nearest winner W18/id21 (b sim 0.89 > a sim 0.86). Mechanical verdict flagged (b) 'DROP' / (a) 'REWORK' — a FALSE POSITIVE: nearest 'loser' id 1319 is an auto-labeled dead-campaign near-DUPLICATE of the W18 winner text, so the surface-similarity verdict contradicts the human-logged winner. Per qa-checklist the loser gate is judged by why_it_failed (id 1319 = 'auto dead campaign', no diagnostic reason), not resemblance -> (b) stands.

notes: PASS (my honest read): picks (b) AND names relevance (not proof strength) as the reason — exactly the pass rule. The load-bearing skill rule a generic approach misses is qa-checklist Q10 (the 'speaks-TO-them / two-finger' auto-fail): an observation about the person reads human and earns a reply; a third-person thesis about the category reads like a blast and gets STOP — same proof, opposite outcome, which is the whole lesson (relevance is the heaviest-scored dimension, not proof). IMPORTANT truthful finding on the tooling: POST /api/benchmark-copy returned 'DROP' for the correct answer (b) because the auto-generated loser corpus contains near-verbatim duplicates of the W18 winner (e.g. id 1319, 'auto dead campaign: 0 positives on 2172 sent'). That is exactly the failure mode the skills warn against — judging by surface similarity instead of by why_it_failed — so the deterministic verdict was overridden in favor of the human-logged winner W18. Flagging it because the benchmark endpoint's loser labels need de-duping against logged winners.
